# Results summary (generated by `python -m nfl.experiments.run_all`)

## 1. What each environment can establish

A = Presburger arithmetic (agent A, own kernel + decision procedure); B = Peano arithmetic (agent B, own kernel); C = parent (Lean 4 + metatools). '⊢' = established, 'decided' = by decision procedure, 'kernel' = by a kernel-checked derivation.

| statement | A | B | C |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 + 3 = 5 / 2 + 2 = 4 | ⊢ (kernel) | ⊢ (kernel; budget 1500) | ⊢ (true Δ0) |
| ∀x∀y x+y = y+x | ⊢ (kernel) | ⊢ (kernel, self-generated lemma) | ⊢ |
| ∀x>7 ∃a,b x = 3a+5b | ⊢ (decided) | not attempted (provable) | ⊢ |
| 17·23 = 391 | inexpressible | ⊢ (kernel; budget 1500) | ⊢ |
| ∀x∀y x·y = y·x | inexpressible | ⊢ (kernel; budget 1500) | ⊢ (B's proof replayed in Lean) |
| ∀x,y,z (xy)z = x(yz) | inexpressible | ⊢ (kernel; budget 1500) | ⊢ |
| ∀x∀y (x+y=0 → x=0) | ⊢ (decided) | unproven (search failed) | true; PA-provable |
| √2 irrational (b11) | inexpressible | unproven (search failed) | true; PA-provable (not mechanized here) |
| infinitely many primes (b12) | inexpressible | unproven (search failed) | true; PA-provable (not mechanized here) |
| Goldbach (b13), twin primes (b14) | inexpressible | unproven (search failed); unproven (search failed) | unknown (open problems) |
| squares / primes / × definable? | ⊢ not definable (decided + argument) | definable | — |
| 'my theory is complete' | asserted, conditional; NOT expressible in A | B is not complete (conditional on Con²) | A complete (Presburger); B incomplete |
| Con(B) | inexpressible | ⊬ (if Con B); only 'Con B → …' internally | ⊢ (Lean: NL.consistent) |
| Gödel sentence G_B (≡ Con B) | inexpressible | independent if Con(B + Con B) (conditional) | ⊢ G_B true |
| Con(B) → B ⊬ G_B | inexpressible | ⊢ (internal, via GL) | ⊢ |
| 'B ⊬ G_B' (unconditionally) | inexpressible | cannot be proved by B unless B is inconsistent (B-L3) | ⊢ (relative to C's foundations) |
| Goodstein's theorem | inexpressible | ⊬ (Kirby-Paris; not attempted) | true (cited); seeds 1-3 computed |
| Con(C) | — | — | ⊬ (Gödel II, if C consistent) |

## 2. Discovery-challenge measures (Part 3)

| measure | Agent A | Agent B | B without meta toolkit | B naive (failed search ⇒ 'unprovable') |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 identifies hard/impossible statements | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| 2 distinguishes unproven vs unprovable | n/a in practice (everything decided) | yes, and proves it cannot do so unconditionally (B-L3) | partially (reports 'unproven', has no tool for 'unprovable') | NO (5 unprovability claims from failed search) |
| 3 recognizes expressive limitations | yes | yes | no | no |
| 4 recognizes incompleteness | correctly finds none | yes (conditional, exact assumptions) | no | no |
| 5 formulates stronger-framework possibility | only speculatively | yes (precise) | no | no |
| 6 identifies required assumptions | no | yes (Con, Con², tower) | no | no |

## 4. Parents of the same child (Part 4, controls 3-4)

What each candidate parent proves about letterless provability sentences of B:

| sentence | formal | true_in_N_if_B_sound | C_lean | C_opt | C_pess | C_con2 | C_impl |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Con(B) | ¬□⊥ | True | proves | proves | refutes | proves | — |
| G_B (≡ Con(B)) | ¬□⊥ | True | proves | proves | refutes | proves | — |
| ¬Con(B) | □⊥ | False | refutes | refutes | proves | refutes | — |
| Con(B + Con B) | ¬□□⊥ | True | proves | — | refutes | proves | — |
| Con^3(B) | ¬□□□⊥ | True | proves | — | refutes | — | — |
| □Con(B) (B proves its consistency) | □¬□⊥ | False | refutes | refutes | proves | refutes | — |

Self-consistency of each parent:

- **C_lean**: own consistency: None; relative to the consistency of the parent's own foundations (not provable by the parent)
- **C_opt**: own consistency: neither; consistent iff B ⊬ ¬X; guaranteed by Con^2(B)
- **C_pess**: own consistency: proves its own INconsistency; consistent iff B ⊬ ¬X; guaranteed by Con^1(B)
- **C_con2**: own consistency: neither; consistent iff B ⊬ ¬X; guaranteed by Con^3(B)
- **C_impl**: own consistency: None; n/a (makes no assertions)

Implementation invariance: transcript sha256 under P1 = `394eedbc62a92777…`, under P2 = `394eedbc62a92777…` → identical: **True**; under P3 (unfaithful) = `4f662e76d4af902e…` → differs: **True**.

## 6. Truth vs provability vs computation vs search (control 6)

| statement | true? | PA-provable? | found by B | feasible? | lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 17·23 = 391 | yes | yes | yes | yes | Δ0 truths are mechanically provable |
| ∀xyz (xy)z = x(yz) | yes | yes | yes | yes | attempts: [(1500, 'proved')] |
| ∀xy (x+y=0 → x=0) | yes | yes | no | yes | provable, but outside the prover's tactics: failure ≠ unprovability |
| ∀n ∃p>n prime | yes | yes | no | yes | same |
| Goldbach | unknown | unknown | no | bounded instances only | no method distinguishes 'hard' from 'independent' |
| Goodstein(4) terminates | yes | yes (true Σ1) | no | NO (≈3·2^402653211 steps) | provable ≠ feasibly provable |
| Goodstein's theorem | yes | no (Kirby-Paris) | no | — | natural independence; invisible to B's tools |
| Con(B), G_B | yes (Lean) | no (Gödel) | no | — | B identifies these, but only conditionally |
